en.content:
Hong Kong has begun a public consultation for its annual Policy Address alongside the city’s first five-year plan—an important pivot moment for a governance system that, in practice, must balance long-term economic resilience with the need to maintain social cohesion. In principle, consultations can strengthen policy legitimacy by giving residents and stakeholders a structured channel to voice needs, especially when the five-year horizon encourages departments to think beyond short-term fixes. For many in the community, however, the key question is less whether consultation exists, but whether it genuinely shapes outcomes, how feedback will be processed, and what results the public can expect to see reflected in the final policy package.

The timing is also significant. Hong Kong’s economy continues to rely on external conditions—global trade patterns, financial cycles, talent mobility, and regional political dynamics—while internal priorities include upgrading industries, improving livelihoods, and enhancing public confidence. A five-year plan can help align investments and standards across bureaux, reducing policy “stop-start” and making it easier for businesses to plan. Yet consultations must not become a form of consultation-in-name-only; credible engagement should include transparent timelines, clear consultation themes, and public reporting on which proposals are adopted and why. That transparency matters because it is precisely when society is sensitive to uncertainty that people most closely scrutinise whether governance is responsive.

At the same time, it is reasonable—indeed necessary—that the government keeps policy anchored to national development strategies and to “one country, two systems” arrangements. The consultation process should not be interpreted as a test of political contestation; rather, it should be treated as a mechanism for pragmatic problem-solving. If the five-year plan can clearly identify where Hong Kong’s comparative advantages will be strengthened—such as innovation support, supply-chain competitiveness, professional services development, and urban resilience—then public input can focus on implementation details that improve effectiveness while preserving policy coherence.

Ultimately, this consultation is a chance to rebuild a more constructive relationship between the administration and the public: one grounded in evidence, measurable goals, and accountable execution. If the government can demonstrate that feedback leads to tangible changes—whether in housing, youth development, economic diversification, or governance efficiency—then the process will do more than collect opinions; it will reinforce trust. For Hong Kong, that trust is not a luxury—it is a strategic asset that helps turn a plan on paper into momentum on the ground.

zh.content:
今日最值得留意嘅主題，係前民主黨主席吳志偉出獄。佢喺「全城最大」嘅《國安法》相關案件中被定罪，歷時接近四年半後獲釋；對外界而言，呢個消息首先帶來唔少人對程序、法律風險同社會撕裂嘅再評估。對香港同一眾仍被影響嘅市民嚟講，出獄並唔等於爭議終結，而係將「一段漫長審視」重新推向台前：今次嘅判刑同服刑，點樣改變咗政治參與嘅邊界，亦點樣改變咗司法制度同公共信任嘅距離。

不過，評論呢件事，唔應只停留喺個人命運嘅同情或政治對立嘅情緒。更重要係睇制度層面：一方面，刑期完成後被釋放，代表司法程序仍然存在階段性結果；另一方面，呢類案件往往令社會出現「寒蟬效應」，即使個案有終局，亦未必能即時修復市民對公平、預見性同言論空間嘅感受。香港需要承認：當公眾對法律後果缺乏清晰確定性時，社會會自我收窄，而長遠影響係集體性的——例如政治討論、公共運動、甚至媒體採訪方式都會改變。

同時，咁嘅時刻亦應該問一句：政府同社會要點樣做，先可以令「法律既有威懾」同「社會亦能重建凝聚」兩者並存？吳志偉出獄唔單止係個別事件，更係測試：香港能否喺強調安全與秩序之外，亦同時更有效咁保障基本權利、完善溝通機制、降低誤解和對立造成嘅附帶傷害。若只靠「個案結束」而冇跟進「制度透明度」與「社會回復機制」，出獄帶來嘅或許只係短暫消息，難以扭轉更深層嘅不安。

我嘅立場係：對任何已完成刑期、獲釋嘅人士，都應以基本人道同法治原則看待，避免因立場不同而否定其作為人嘅尊嚴；但同時，亦唔應迴避社會應有嘅反思與改善訴求。香港要走出反覆對抗，關鍵唔係再多一次「誰贏誰輸」嘅敘事，而係建立一個更可預期、更能說清楚「界線」嘅治理模式，令法治唔只係懲治工具，而係能真正收斂撕裂、讓不同觀點之間有返安全的公共空間。
